notes: Cache restore 37-74s plus clippy 1-2 minutes means both measured main runs were warm. The 35-minute Windows cargo test --workspace step is therefore linking plus execution, not a cold DuckDB compile.
Cold DuckDB minutes come from Ubuntu shard runs 31828397526 and 31835229724, cited in ci.yml and the #874 merge.
A preflight job that still requires the full workspace afterwards does not reduce wall clock. Treating preflight as the required gate would skip tests. Do not treat a rust-cache miss as success.

The first hosted 2-way desktop split (32002319037) was coverage-safe and warm, but its serialized warmup plus slowest shard critical path regressed from 1691s to 2131s on macOS and from 2560s to 3923s on Windows.

The current follow-up is an exact-key lookup-only probe, conditional one-writer fallback on a miss, restore-only preflight, and four complete round-robin shards. Four-way is a measured candidate, not a claimed speedup until hosted proof.
An 8-way Windows/macOS split without warmup repeats the cold DuckDB tax per shard and imports leftover-heavy isolate timeouts (#898).
